decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Metagross. Lead Whimsicott Tailwind + Metagross Ice Punch targets Garchomp 4x weak to Ice; Mega Tough Claws guarantees OHKO. Tailwind lets Metagross outspeed Rotom-Wash to attack first. Back Archaludon Thunderbolts Talonflame and pressures Water types; Quaquaval Liquidation + Moxie snowballs through Garchomp/Rotom-Wash remnants and handles Dark/Steel. Steel resist Fairy for Floette-Eternal switch-ins.
decisions.notebook: Game 3, series tied 1-1. Opponent leads Garchomp (LO, Rough Skin) + Rotom-Wash (Sitrus Berry) consistently. Garchomp Protects vs double targets. Rotom-Wash uses Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp. Back threats: Floette-Eternal (Floettite, Light of Ruin 140 BP, Protect/Synthesis stall), Talonflame (Gale Wings priority Brave Bird full HP, Sharp Beak), Dragapult (Focus Sash, Infiltrator bypasses screens, Phantom Force), Annihilape (Leftovers, Defiant boosts on stat drops, Close Combat SE vs Steel). Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind can fail; preserve it. Archaludon Draco Meteor drops SpA -2, use sparingly. Metagross Mega is primary win condition; Ice Punch 4x SE on Garchomp, Meteor Mash for Fairy/Ice. Quaquaval Moxie snowballs on KOs. Grimmsnarl screens + Parting Shot for momentum if needed. Stunfisk-Galar Thunder Wave + Mimicry situational.

decisions.rationale: Floette-Rotom lead pressures the expected Grimmsnarl+Stunfisk with special STAB that ignores Reflect. Rotom Volt Switch pivots into Garchomp, whose Life Orb EQ OHKOs Metagross-Mega and threatens Archaludon. Annihilape's Defiant deters Parting Shot and cleans late-game with Rage Fist. All four are immune to or resist Stunfisk's EQ, preserving momentum against the paralysis mode.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Opponent brought Grimmsnarl (Careful, Light Clay, Reflect/Light Screen/Spirit Break/Parting Shot) and Stunfisk-Galar (Impish, Leftovers, EQ/Crunch/Thunder Wave/Protect) after sitting Game 2. Grimmsnarl likely HP/SpD invested—Moonblast range 68-166%, not guaranteed OHKO. Stunfisk Hydro Pump range 73-168%. Metagross-Mega resists Fairy (Light of Ruin 0.5x); Garchomp remains primary answer. Whimsicott outspeeds Floette (Timid 184 vs 158) plus Prankster on status. Opponent favors Tailwind+Encore disruption into offensive backline. Annihilape Defiant deters Parting Shot pivots.

decisions.rationale: Meteor Mash has 90.1% minimum to OHKO Floette-Eternal removing the 140BP Light of Ruin threat which is the biggest danger. Earthquake spread is less reliable (42.7% min vs Rotom) and leaves Floette alive to spam Fairy moves.

decisions.rationale: Tailwind gives both foes speed advantage. Garchomp cannot survive Ice Punch reliably (77-150%). Protect blocks all incoming damage at +4 priority before Encore locks it. No other line preserves Garchomp while removing Metagross.

reflections.summary: Metagross-Mega's Ice Punch and Whimsicott's Moonblast cleanly removed Annihilape and Garchomp, while Archaludon's Thunderbolt finished Rotom-Wash. Prankster Tailwind secured speed control throughout.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Quaquaval with a Grass-type or direct Rotom-Wash answer, as it was KO'd by Volt Switch without meaningful contribution.
reflections.notebook: Series won 2-1. Opponent sets: Rotom-Wash (Sitrus, Modest, Hydro Pump/Volt Switch/Will-O-Wisp/Protect) bulky pivot; Garchomp (Life Orb, Jolly, Rough Skin); Annihilape (Leftovers, Jolly, Defiant); Floette-Eternal (Floettite, Timid, Flower Veil); Talonflame (Sharp Beak, Jolly, Gale Wings); Dragapult (Focus Sash, Adamant, Infiltrator). Opponent leads Annihilape/Garchomp, spams Protect. Whimsicott+Metagross handles early game; Archaludon checks Rotom. Future: replace Quaquaval with Grass-type for Rotom answer.

reflections.summary: Game was lost because Whimsicott's Tailwind and Encore dominated the tempo. Early double targeting KOed Annihilape, then Garchomp fell after a failed double Protect, leaving Rotom-Wash alone against a boosted Archaludon and Whimsicott. Floette was likely removed early or could not break through the opponent's Steel-types. The combination of speed control and Encore punishment for repeated moves left us unable to regain momentum.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, reconsider team preview: bring a dedicated speed control option (Tailwind or Trick Room) to match Whimsicott. Avoid Pokémon that rely heavily on Protect or repeated moves against Encore. Consider a lead that can pressure Whimsicott immediately (e.g., Fake Out, fast Taunt, or strong Fairy-resistant offense). Prioritize eliminating Whimsicott or its partner before Tailwind goes up. If Floette is brought, ensure it has support to handle Steel types.
reflections.notebook: Game 3 loss. Opponent consistently leads Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster Encore + Tailwind) with a strong attacker (Metagross-Mega or Archaludon). Whimsicott uses Encore proactively to punish defensive moves. Metagross-Mega often carries Ice Punch for Dragons and will trade with Rough Skin. Archaludon (Modest, Expert Belt, Stalwart) threatens special hits and ignores redirection. Opponent plays aggressively, prioritizing early KOs. Our team struggles significantly under Tailwind without speed control; Floette-Eternal is walled by Steel types. Future games require a speed control plan and an answer to Whimsicott right from team preview.
